title: Shortest Corridor Route (Graph BFS)
real_world_story: A warehouse robot has finished its pick and must get back to the charging dock. The building is a network of rooms joined by corridors, and the controller needs the smallest number of corridors the robot must pass through.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Rooms and the corridors joining them
real_world_connection.query_represents: The robot room and the charging dock room
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Spreading level by level through rooms until the dock is reached

problem_statement: Given N rooms numbered 0 to N-1 and E undirected corridors, plus a robot room S and a charging dock room G, find the minimum number of corridors the robot must pass through to reach the dock.
task: Return the minimum number of corridors from S to G, or -1 if the dock cannot be reached.
input_format: The first line contains three integers N, M and D with D = 0 for undirected corridors and D = 1 for one-way doorways. The next M lines each contain two integers u v. The final line contains two integers S and G.
output_format: Print the minimum number of corridors from S to G, or -1 if unreachable. Print 0 when S and G are the same room.

examples.explanation: From room 0 the robot can go 0 -> 1 -> 2 or 0 -> 3 -> 2, so 2 corridors is the shortest route to room 2.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph BFS
expected_algorithm.reason: Every corridor costs exactly one move, so visiting rooms level by level guarantees the first time the dock is reached its distance is the shortest possible.

complexity.time: O(N + M) because every room and corridor is processed once
complexity.space: O(N + M) for the adjacency list and the queue

hint: Store the rooms in an adjacency list with one list per room.
Process rooms in a queue and record the distance of each newly found room.
Reverse the neighbour order only when doorways are one-way; undirected corridors go both ways.
real_world_takeaway: When every corridor costs the same, breadth-first search answers 'which route is shortest?' without measuring every route.
